glosses: loss, losing (in a game or war)

examples.text: Он засну́л почти́ в по́лдень и спал тем тяжёлым сном без сновиде́ний, кото́рым спи́тся то́лько о́чень молодо́му челове́ку и по́сле о́чень большо́го про́игрыша.
examples.translation: It was nearly noon when he fell asleep and he had slept that heavy dreamless sleep which only very young men sleep after a heavy loss.
examples.english: It was nearly noon when he fell asleep and he had slept that heavy dreamless sleep which only very young men sleep after a heavy loss.

examples.text: Хороший игрок, проигравший в шахматы, искренно убежден, что его проигрыш произошел от его ошибки, и он отыскивает эту ошибку в начале своей игры, но забывает, что в каждом его шаге, в продолжение всей игры, были такие же ошибки, что ни один его ход не был совершенен.
Порой победы так не объединяют, как поражения. Но не заурядный проигрыш, а такой момент в жизни команды, когда все выкладываются, бьются, а результата нет.

glosses: то, что проиграно, проигранная сумма

examples.text: Часто играли в карты, ― в пикет и в шестьдесят шесть, ― и непременно на деньги, а проигрыш приписывали к старым карточным долгам, которые иногда достигали десятков тысяч рублей.
Проигрыш был крупный ― около 6000 рублей, то есть примерно двухлетнее жалование этого инженера.

glosses: муз. часть музыкального сопровождения песни, не сопровождаемая пением

examples.text: Приглашённый бард настроил гитару и запел что-то отвечающее настроению и интеллектуальному уровню компании — что-то из фантастической жизни. Смешно. То и дело все дружно хохотали, а он в это время делал проигрыш.

translations.source_sense_description: неблагоприятный, неудачный для кого-либо исход игры, соревнования

glosses: The result of no longer possessing an object, a function, or a characteristic due to external causes or misplacement.

examples.text: loss of limb; weight loss; loss of cognitive functions; loss of appetite.
In other areas, glacier loss creates serious risk of a dry period across the Third Pole, Wang said.

glosses: The destruction or ruin of an object.
Something that has been destroyed or ruined.

examples.text: It was a terrible crash; both cars were total losses.

glosses: Defeat; an instance of being defeated.

examples.text: The match ended in their first loss of the season.

glosses: The death of a person or animal.

examples.text: We mourn his loss.
The battle was won, but losses were great.

glosses: The condition of grief caused by losing someone or something, especially someone who has died.

examples.text: Her daughter's sense of loss eventually led to depression.

glosses: The sum an entity loses on balance.

examples.text: The sum of expenditures and taxes minus total income is a loss, when this difference is positive.

glosses: Electricity of kinetic power expended without doing useful work.

examples.text: The inefficiency of many old-fashioned power plants exceeds 60% loss before the subsequent losses during transport over the grid.

glosses: Alternative spelling of lost.

translations.source_sense_description: неблагоприятный, неудачный для кого-либо исход игры, соревнования

glosses: To overcome in battle or contest.

examples.text: Wellington defeated Napoleon at Waterloo.

The Japanese defeated the Ming general Tsu Chʻeng-hsün 祖承訓 at Pʻing jang 平壤 in 1592, the first year of Bunroku 文祿 of Japan, and the fighting continued for some years; but at Hideyoshi's death the Japanese troops left Korea.

My personal success or failure is insignificant; the rise or fall of the nation is my responsibility and must not be shirked. Upon introspection, I feel I am firmer than ever in confidence that the Communists will be defeated. These are feelings which will comfort Father's soul in Heaven.

glosses: To reduce, to nothing, the strength of.

examples.text: He finds himself naturally to dread a superior Being that can defeat all his designs, and disappoint all his hopes.
In one instance he defeated his own purpose.

glosses: To nullify

examples.text: The escheators […] defeated the right heir of his succession.

glosses: To prevent (something) from being achieved.

examples.text: The last active L.Y.R. 0-6-0ST (apart from works shunters), No. 51408, has been moved from Bolton to Agecroft for use in New Bailey Yard, Salford, where a sharp 1 in 27 curve is said to have defeated all attempts so far to employ diesel shunters; an ex-L.Y.R. 0-4-0ST also works here.

glosses: The act or instance of being defeated, of being overcome or vanquished; a loss.

examples.text: Licking their wounds after a temporary defeat, they planned their next move.

glosses: The act or instance of defeating, of overcoming, vanquishing.

examples.text: The inscription records her defeat of the country's enemies in a costly war.

glosses: Frustration (by prevention of success), stymieing; (law) nullification.

examples.text: ... is subsequently issued to him, in accordance with his perfect equity thus acquired, by a legal fiction which the law creates for the protection, but not for the defeat, of his title.
